content:
We're back with another round of picks from Apple's official certified refurbished store. This channel is gaining more attention for saving money on iPhones, MacBooks, Studio Displays, and Apple TVs—we're not talking about some guy's cousin piecing together iPhones from parts and reselling them, but rather units that go through Apple's "rigorous refurbishment process" and come with a full one-year Apple warranty.

Read on for a closer look at what we added to our carts this week—iPhones, MacBooks, Studio Displays, and more.

Apple Refurbished Store – Weekly Picks

***Apple Certified Refurbished product availability may be very limited

Justin – iPhone 16 Plus, Pro, and Max

Sure, you can find cheaper renewed iPhone 16 Pros on Amazon, but when it comes to refurbished iPhones, I much prefer an Apple-certified source. Apart from AirPods, the iPhone is probably the easiest Apple product to scratch or drop among the most widely used ones, so I'd definitely go straight to Apple for an unlocked refurbished iPhone, which of course comes with a full one-year Apple warranty.

The Apple Refurbished Store has plenty of iPhone 16 series models in stock—if you ask me, this phone will serve you well for years to come—starting from $699, and I noticed that the 1TB 16 Pro Max is only $1,269. That's a full $330 cheaper than the equivalent 17 Pro Max, and even $130 cheaper than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 starting from $699 (up to $330 off vs. 17 series)

Chance – MacBook Air

The MacBook Air is my top recommendation for friends and family looking to buy a new Mac. It's available in 13-inch and 15-inch (my personal favourite) screen sizes, with a great range of RAM and storage configurations to suit different workflows. Right now, the best place to find MacBook Air deals is Apple's refurbished store:

  • 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 1TB storage and 16GB memory: $1,359 (original new price $1,599)
  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air with 1TB storage and 16GB memory: $1,529 (original new price $1,799)
  • …plus more configuration options…

Zac – 48GB RAM MacBook Pro

Looking to save money while maxing out memory? Apple's refurbished MacBook Pro lineup includes five models with 48GB of RAM. The 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro is by far the best value for users with high memory demands—such as running local AI models—priced well below $3,000.

Other 48GB RAM configurations feature newer, more powerful Apple Silicon, nano-texture glass, and more CPU and GPU cores. The 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 48GB RAM is priced at $2,719, which is incredibly attractive for users with high memory demands.

Marcus – Studio Display XDR

After a long wait, the Apple Studio Display XDR is finally available in the company's certified refurbished store. Although this display sidestepped Apple's recent price hikes, its base pricing is already not cheap. So the roughly 15% refurbished discount is indeed welcome news, especially for users looking to upgrade their setup with Apple's 27-inch 5K display—this screen supports P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts and features a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR – Standard Glass – VESA Mount Adapter: $2,459 (original price $2,899)
  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR – Standard Glass – Tilt and Height-Adjustable Stand: $2,799 (original price $3,299)
  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR – Nano-texture Glass – Tilt and Height-Adjustable Stand: $3,059 (original price $3,599)

Jeff – Apple Studio Display

The Studio Display XDR mentioned above, while clearly the more appealing of the two displays Apple currently sells, has the standard Studio Display priced a full $1,100 cheaper than this higher-end version in the Apple Refurbished Store.

What's the main selling point of the standard Studio Display? It's the minimalist all-metal and glass design. Although it lacks specs like high refresh rate support, AdobeRGB, and mini-LED backlighting, it has recently been upgraded with dual Thunderbolt 5 ports, finally supporting daisy-chain configurations. While it certainly isn't the most cost-effective display in terms of value, in terms of design aesthetics, it's truly in a class of its own.

  • Refurbished Studio Display – Standard Glass – Tilt-Adjustable Stand $1,359 (original price $1,599)

Ben – MacBook Neo

The MacBook Neo is the newest addition, and for many users, it's more than sufficient as a Mac for everyday use. It received a $100 price hike not long after launch, but buying through the Apple Refurbished Store lets you get it at the original pricing.

  • Base model (no Touch ID): $599 (original new price $699)
  • Touch ID model: $679 (original new price $799)
  • The above links are for silver versions; all colour options can be found here
